sheets.title: Mauryan empire (322 – 185 BCE)
sheets.intro: Chandragupta to Brihadratha: rulers, edicts, state, economy, art, decline.

keys.name: Sources

rows.v: Kautilya; Sanskrit; 15 books, 180 chapters, 3 parts; found 1905, published 1909 by R. Shamasastry
Megasthenes (Seleucus's envoy at Pataliputra); lost, only quoted fragments
Vishakhadatta (Gupta age) – drama on Nanda's fall
Buddhist texts (Divyavadana, Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa), Jain Parishishtaparvan (Hemachandra), Puranas; Pliny (army size)
39 Ashokan edicts; Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman (150 CE)
NBPW, punch-marked coins, Kumhrar hall

traps: Arthashastra – Kautilya; Indica – Megasthenes; Mudrarakshasa – Vishakhadatta

keys.name: Chandragupta Maurya

rows.v: 322 – 297 BCE; Pataliputra
With Chanakya overthrew Dhana Nanda (322/321 BCE)
Brahmanical – son of a Shudra woman (Mura); Buddhist – Moriya Kshatriya clan of Pipphalivana (Gorakhpur)
Beat Seleucus I Nicator 305 BCE – got Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Baluchistan), Paropamisadae (Kabul), Aria (Herat); gave 500 elephants; marriage pact; Megasthenes sent
Pliny – 6,00,000 foot, 30,000 horse, 9,000 elephants
All north and NW, Bengal, Odisha, Deccan; only Kerala, Tamil Nadu, parts of NE outside
Governor Pushyagupta built Sudarshana lake, Girnar (Junagadh inscription)
Jain monk under Bhadrabahu; Sallekhana at Chandragiri hill, Shravanabelagola

traps: Chandragupta Maurya (322 BCE) ≠ Chandragupta I Gupta (319 CE)

rows.v: Chanakya, Kautilya, Vishnugupta
Planned Nanda's fall; PM of Chandragupta and Bindusara
Yogakshema (welfare duty of king); Saptanga theory; spies; strong central rule

keys.name: Bindusara

rows.v: Amitraghata / Amitrochates, Allitrochates ("slayer of foes")
South up to Mysore; 16 states (Taranatha); only Kalinga left
Asked Antiochus I (Syria) for sweet wine, figs and a sophist; envoys Deimachus (Antiochus I) and Dionysius (Ptolemy II, Egypt)
Taxila revolted – sent prince Ashoka
Ajivika

traps: Antiochus I = Bindusara’s friend; Antiochus II = named in Ashoka’s edicts

rows.v: c. 268 – 232 BCE (accession 272/273, crowned c. 268)
Viceroy at Ujjain; sent to Taxila revolt
Devanampiya Piyadasi; name "Ashoka" only at Maski, Nittur, Udegolam (Karnataka), Gujarra (MP); "Ranyo Ashoka" portrait at Kanganahalli
Buddhist through Upagupta (also Nigrodha); 3rd council 250 BCE (Moggaliputta Tissa)
Son Mahinda (Mahendra), daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka; others to Burma, West Asia
Dhamma Mahamattas (13th year); Rajukas (reward and punish; land survey); rotated officers at Ujjain, Taxila, Tosali
Tushaspha (Yavana) added canals to Sudarshana lake
Karuvaki (Queen's Edict)
"First global ambassador of India"

keys.name: Kalinga war

rows.v: 261 BCE (8th year of reign)
Coastal Odisha
1,00,000 killed, 1,50,000 deported (Rock Edict XIII)
Bherighosha (war drum) → Dhammaghosha (drum of Dhamma)
Separate Kalinga Edict (Dhauli, Jaugada) – "All men are my children"

traps: Kalinga 261 BCE; Seleucus war 305 BCE; Ashoka died 232 BCE

rows.v: Moral code for all – not a conversion to Buddhism
Respect elders, kindness to slaves and animals, tolerance of all sects, few rituals
Paternal – subjects as children
Dhamma Mahamattas; Dhammayatras (tours) replacing hunts; tours every 5 years by Yuktas, Rajukas, Pradeshikas
Medical care for men and animals; wells, trees, rest houses

keys.name: 14 Major Rock Edicts

rows.v: Ban on animal sacrifice and samajas (festive gatherings)
Medical care for men, animals; names Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, Keralaputras, Tamraparni (Sri Lanka)
Yuktas, Rajukas, Pradeshikas tour every 5 years
Bherighosha → Dhammaghosha
Dhamma Mahamattas appointed
King to be told of public affairs at all times
Tolerance of all sects ("who praises his own sect … harms it")
Dhammayatras; visit to Bodh Gaya
Against useless rituals; true glory is Dhamma; explains Dhamma
Kalinga war; names 5 Greek kings – Antiochus II (Syria), Ptolemy II (Egypt), Antigonus (Macedonia), Magas (Cyrene), Alexander (Epirus)
Why the edicts were carved
Dhauli, Jaugada drop RE XI – XIII; add 2 Separate Kalinga Edicts

traps: RE I = no sacrifice; RE XIII = Kalinga

rows.v: 7; PE V – animals not to be killed, 25 prisoners freed; PE VI – Dhamma; PE VII longest (only Delhi-Topra, moved by Firoz Tughlaq)
Queen's Edict, Schism Edict; later Samudragupta's prashasti, Jahangir's record
Faith in Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha
Buddha's birthplace; village freed of bali, bhaga cut to 1/8
Minor Rock Edicts I, II
Greek – Aramaic bilingual
Famine relief (Mauryan)

keys.name: Edict languages and sites

rows.v: Prakrit in Brahmi
Kharosthi – Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra (Pakistan)
Greek and Aramaic (Kandahar)
James Prinsep, 1837 (Brahmi)
Erragudi (Kurnool) – Major Rock Edicts; Rajula Mandagiri (Kurnool) – Minor RE; Amaravati – pillar fragment
Dhauli, Jaugada (Odisha); Kalsi (Uttarakhand); Girnar (Gujarat); Sopara (Maharashtra)
Chunar sandstone, one piece, polished

traps: Jaugada and Dhauli are in Odisha; Kalsi in Uttarakhand

rows.v: 232 – 224 BCE; Ashoka's grandson; Nagarjuni caves to Ajivikas
224 – 215 BCE; great Jain patron
Shalishuka, Devavarman, Shatadhanvan
187 – 185 BCE; killed by general Pushyamitra Shunga at a parade
All power; council (Mantriparishad) advice not binding
Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, Mitra
Top officers – Mantrin, Purohita, Senapati, Yuvaraja; pay 48,000 panas down to 60 panas
Collector-general of revenue (assessment)
Treasurer, storehouses
Dharmasthiya (civil, Vyavaharika); Kantakashodhana (criminal, Pradeshta)
Gudhapurushas – samstha (fixed) and sanchara (wandering)
Taxila
Ujjain
Suvarnagiri
Tosali (Dhauli)
Pataliputra
Princes – Kumara, Aryaputra; Rashtrapala
Pradeshika (like DM); Rajuka (survey, land); Yukta (revenue clerk); Sthanika (collector); Gopa (accounts, 5 – 10 villages)
Agoranomoi (district), Astynomoi (city)
6 boards of 5 members (Megasthenes) – crafts, foreigners, births and deaths, trade, goods, tax on sales
6 boards of 5 – infantry, cavalry, elephants, chariots, navy, transport
Nagaraka
80-pillar hall (Patna)

keys.name: Economy and tax

rows.v: State ran mines, liquor, arms (monopolies); state farms (Sita land) worked by slaves and hired labour
27 adhyakshas – Sitadhyaksha (crown farms), Panyadhyaksha (trade), Lakshanadhyaksha (mint), Sunadhyaksha (slaughter), Navadhyaksha (ships), Sulkadhyaksha (customs)
Bhaga 1/4 to 1/6 of produce; Bali; Pindakara (lump village tax); in kind too; extra cultivation in emergency
Punch-marked silver (peacock, hill and crescent) – pana; copper mashaka

traps: Land tax ranged 1/4 to 1/6 – not a flat 1/6

rows.v: 7 castes – philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, overseers, councillors
Said India had no slavery and no famine (Arthashastra shows slaves)
Iron tools, NBPW, punch-marked coins, burnt bricks (first in NE India), ring wells (first in Ganga plain), spoked wheel, writing

keys.name: Mauryan art

rows.v: Chunar buff sandstone, monolithic, mirror polish
4 lions back to back; abacus – elephant, horse, bull, lion with wheels; 24-spoke chakra; emblem 26 Jan 1950 with "Satyameva Jayate"
Bull – Rampurva; lion – Lauriya Nandangarh (whole pillar); elephant – Sankisa
Barabar (Lomas Rishi, Sudama) – Ajivikas; Nagarjuni (Dasharatha)
Didarganj Yakshi (chauri bearer, polished) – near Patna
Sanchi, Bharhut cores

traps: Lion capital = Sarnath; bull capital = Rampurva
Lion capital is Mauryan, not Gupta

rows.v: Anti-sacrifice policy hurt priests (H.P. Shastri)
Huge army, staff, gifts to monks; gold images melted (R.S. Sharma)
Taxila revolts
Iron and skills spread – new powers (Shungas, Kanvas, Chedis, Satavahanas)
No wall, passes open to Greeks, Shakas
Empire split after 232 BCE
Brihadratha killed by Pushyamitra Shunga, 185 BCE
